question: What is the primary goal of home health nursing?
explanation: Home health nursing focuses on empowering clients to manage their health conditions safely at home. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h1)

question: Home health nurses typically experience more of which working condition than hospital nurses?

options.C: Routine access to immediate lab support

explanation: Working outside the hospital requires home health nurses to rely heavily on independent judgment during home visits. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which task is a standard core responsibility of the home health nurse?

options.A: Prescribing new medications without a doctor
options.B: Purchasing all household groceries for the patient
options.C: Performing major surgical operations at home
options.D: Managing wound care and monitoring vital signs

explanation: Direct clinical tasks like dressing wounds and tracking vital signs form the basis of daily home health nursing duties. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h2)

question: Why is medication management a critical duty for home health nurses?

options.A: Patients often mix up prescriptions or miss doses without support
options.B: Family members never want to participate in drug administration
options.C: Pharmacies refuse to deliver medications to private residences
options.D: Nurses are legally required to manufacture pills inside the home

explanation: Organizing medications and checking adherence prevents harmful drug errors and avoidable hospital readmissions. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h2)

question: What makes home assessment unique compared to hospital assessment?

options.A: It evaluates environmental hazards in the living space
options.B: It ignores physical vital signs entirely
options.C: It is performed exclusively by attending physicians
options.D: It requires advanced laboratory equipment on site

explanation: Home assessments specifically incorporate living conditions like lighting and flooring that impact patient safety. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h3)

question: Who should be involved in co-creating the home health care plan?
explanation: Involving the patient and family ensures the care plan is practical and achievable in daily life. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h3)

question: What is a major technical challenge when performing procedures at home?

options.A: Relying entirely on hospital central sterile supply
options.B: Performing procedures without any medical equipment
options.C: Maintaining strict infection control in a variable environment
options.D: Having too many sterile surgical tables available

explanation: Home environments lack the controlled sterility of hospital rooms, requiring nurses to adapt infection control practices carefully. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h4)

question: A home nurse needs to change a urinary catheter on a bed with poor lighting. What is the best action?

options.A: Use a portable examination light and position supplies safely
options.B: Cancel the procedure until the patient goes to the hospital
options.C: Ask the family members to hold regular flashlights directly
options.D: Perform the procedure in total darkness using touch only

explanation: Resourcefulness and proper equipment adaptation allow nurses to perform sterile procedures safely in homes. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h4)

question: Which communication technique helps confirm that a patient actually understands health instructions?

options.D: Asking closed yes or no questions

explanation: Having patients repeat instructions in their own words verifies their true comprehension. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why is family education crucial in home health care?

options.A: Nurses are only present for brief intermittent visits
options.B: Families are legally liable for all nursing errors
options.C: Patients cannot learn anything new while sick
options.D: Hospitals forbid nurses from educating patients directly

explanation: Because nurses leave after short visits, families must be equipped to handle routine care and recognize warning signs. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which role does the home health nurse frequently assume within the multidisciplinary team?
explanation: The nurse often serves as the central hub connecting the various health professionals visiting the home. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why is regular communication among multidisciplinary team members essential in home care?

options.A: It guarantees that doctors never have to visit patients
options.B: It reduces the total number of required home visits to zero
options.C: It prevents duplicated efforts and ensures holistic support
options.D: It eliminates the need for patient and family involvement

explanation: Sharing observations across disciplines ensures all care aspects align safely toward common patient goals. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h6)

question: How should a home health nurse handle a competent patient refusing a recommended treatment?

options.A: Force the treatment immediately against their expressed wishes
options.B: Respect patient autonomy while providing education on risks
options.C: Abandon the case and never return to the household
options.D: Call the police to arrest the patient for non-compliance

explanation: Competent patients retain the legal right to make choices about their care, requiring nurses to balance education with respect for autonomy. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h7)

question: Which factor represents a common personal safety risk for community health nurses?

options.A: Handling strictly controlled clinical laboratory equipment
options.B: Entering unfamiliar neighborhoods and private homes
options.C: Exposure to sterile hospital operating room air systems
options.D: Working under constant direct supervision of surgeons

explanation: Community nursing requires entering unmonitored private spaces where safety hazards can be unpredictable. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h7)
